LoloBuy Spreadsheet Guide: How to Find and Check Products Before Ordering

Independent buyer guide

A LoloBuy spreadsheet can help you find a product, but a saved link is only the beginning of the decision. The listing may have changed, the photographed item may represent a different option, and the price displayed during research may not include delivery or later parcel costs. Use the spreadsheet to build a shortlist, then verify the live listing and retain the evidence needed for a warehouse check.

This independent guide explains a practical sequence: find a category, check a seller’s listing, record the exact choice, review available warehouse evidence, and plan a parcel using the live information shown for your destination. It does not guarantee availability, authenticity, fit, price or delivery.

What a spreadsheet is useful for

A product spreadsheet or directory brings together paths to product listings. It can help you compare a few candidates without starting every search from scratch. Begin with a category such as shoes, hoodies or jackets, then search for the item’s useful characteristics: product type, colour, material description, size range or intended use. A more precise search often gives you a smaller set of listings to investigate.

Treat the row as a pointer, not as an independent product inspection. A photo, price or seller note may have been collected at a different time. Stock may change and a link may lead to a different variation from the one pictured. Open the current product record and check whether the relevant source listing still matches what you intended to research.

Before comparing options, write down the criteria that matter. For a jacket these could be chest width, back length, colour and a maximum item budget. For shoes they may include the size chart, visible construction and the version shown in the listing. Keeping a short list makes a low price less likely to distract you from a missing measurement or an unsuitable option.

Compare the live listing with the spreadsheet

Open the seller or source record when it is available and compare it with the discovery page. Does the product name describe the same item? Are the photographs consistent? Are the intended colour, size and quantity actually selectable? If an option is unavailable or a page cannot be opened, mark that uncertainty instead of assuming an old row remains accurate.

Check the listing’s unit and bundle carefully. One thumbnail may represent a single item, while the price may correspond to an accessory, a different size or a different version. Translation can also make two options sound similar. Preserve the seller’s original option text or code alongside your own translation so that you can compare the two later.

Compare like with like. A listing for a lightweight item may appear cheaper than a heavier version, but the pictures alone may not establish the fabric, dimensions or included parts. If the difference matters, record the question and seek clarification before paying. Do not turn a seller description into a claim that the product has been independently tested.

Make a useful product record

For each shortlisted product, save the source URL, seller name or identifier, date checked, chosen option, quantity, displayed item price and size chart. Retain any relevant size diagram or screenshot, subject to the platform’s rules and your own privacy. Note which details are confirmed by the listing and which are still unclear.

A simple record might say: “jacket; black; seller option code B; size L; one item; chest width shown on seller chart; measurement method not stated.” If the seller later changes the listing, that record preserves the choice you were trying to make. It also gives you a basis for asking a specific question instead of relying on memory.

Keep sensitive information out of anything shared publicly. An order number, payment confirmation, address or full tracking number is not needed to ask a community whether a measurement is visible in a photograph. Use the platform’s account-specific support channel for personal transaction details.

Understand item payment and international shipping separately

LoloBuy’s public pages describe a workflow that starts with a product link and includes warehouse inspection and international shipping. A product listing can show the item price or an estimate before the parcel is ready. That figure should not automatically be read as a delivered total. The seller-to-warehouse stage and the later international parcel stage are different decisions.

Build a budget in layers: item price; any domestic delivery or payment charges shown for the order; optional warehouse services you actually select; international freight and packaging; and destination taxes, duties or carrier handling charges where applicable. Some amounts may not be known until the products are packed and measured. Keep unknown amounts as unknown rather than inserting a figure copied from another buyer’s parcel.

When comparing shipping options, use quotes for the same destination, parcel contents, weight and dimensions. Check the date of each quote and whether it includes the services you need. A route available to one address, product type or parcel may not be offered for another. Read the current route conditions and item restrictions before selecting a line.

Use warehouse photos to answer specific questions

When inspection photographs are available, compare them with the record of what you ordered. First check the overall item, quantity, colour and any visible option or size label. Then look for the feature you recorded as important: for example, whether a jacket’s front and back appear consistent with the listing, or whether both shoes show the same visible size label.

If a photograph does not show the detail that would change your decision, consider asking for a more specific view where the live service offers one. Write one clear request for each view. For a measurement, name the two endpoints, the unit and how the item should be laid out. Ask for the scale and both endpoints to be visible in the same image. Check the displayed price and conditions before confirming an optional service.

Photographs have limits. They can document visible features; they cannot by themselves establish authenticity, material composition, hidden damage, durability, electronic performance or how an item will fit your body. If a scale is obscured or a photograph uses a different measurement method from the seller’s chart, treat the result as inconclusive.

What to do when something does not match

Do not submit an international parcel while an important item question remains unresolved. Preserve the original option record, relevant listing details and warehouse images. Describe the observed difference factually: the ordered option, what the label or image appears to show, and the specific clarification you need. If the discrepancy involves a measurement, include the endpoints, units and seller’s measurement method if known.

The available resolution depends on the order stage, seller terms and current platform rules. A photograph that looks different is not automatic proof that a return is available. Ask support what options apply to the particular item before taking the next irreversible step, and retain the response together with your order record.

Plan the parcel and keep the evidence

Once you are satisfied with the items, review the proposed contents together. Check restrictions for the destination and shipping line, especially for goods that require special handling. Consider whether original boxes, protective materials or consolidation change the parcel’s weight and size. Check the current quote after selecting the relevant options; an earlier estimate may have used different dimensions or assumptions.

For shipments to the Netherlands or another destination, identify which costs are already collected and which may be requested later. Rules, thresholds and carrier charges change, so verify the current guidance for your own order rather than relying on an old spreadsheet note. Retain invoices and the final parcel description for your records. If a payment message arrives later, verify it through the carrier’s independently opened official channel rather than following an unexpected link.

A final checklist before you proceed

  1. Open the live product record and confirm that the source, item and selected option still match.
  2. Record the seller’s size method, option code, quantity and item price; mark anything uncertain.
  3. Distinguish the item order and domestic delivery from the later international parcel.
  4. Review available inspection photos against your record and request a precise additional view only if it would help your decision.
  5. Compare parcel options for the same contents and destination, and account for charges that may appear later.
  6. Keep order evidence privately and use official support for account-specific questions.

The aim is not to make every purchase complicated. It is to give each decision a reliable reference point. A useful LoloBuy spreadsheet helps you find candidates; the live listing, your order record, warehouse evidence and final parcel quote each answer a different question.
